turns.t: Hi, doctor, sorry, we're a bit rushed, I've got the other two in the car with their dad. This is Ollie, he's eight, and he won't eat anything.
Hello Ollie. What do you eat, if I ask you? ~
Pasta. Plain. And chicken nuggets. And toast.
Anything green? ~
No. Yuck. ~
How long has the pickiness been going on, Mum?
Six months, since he started Year 4. He used to eat fruit and a bit of veg.
Two months. It's not six. I stopped liking things at Easter.
So Ollie says two months and Mum says six months. We'll write two to six. Ollie, does your tummy hurt when you eat?
No. ~
He's never complained about his tummy. He just says no. ~
Any problems with how he's growing, Mum? Is he energetic? ~
He's a bit tired after school, but he plays football like a maniac. ~
Any allergies, to food or medicine?
No allergies at all.
Right, let's weigh and measure him. Ollie, stand up straight against the wall. ~
Okay.
Weight 21.5 kilos, height 118 centimetres, BMI 15.4. Pulse 86, temperature 36.7.
Is he underweight? ~
He's at the lower end of normal for his age, but he's on his growth line, and he's grown since the last time he was measured. ~
That's a relief. ~
Do the other two eat well? ~
Yes, the younger one eats everything. He's the odd one. ~
Fussy eating is very common in this age group, and as long as he's growing and has energy, I'm not worried. I'd say this is most likely simple picky eating.
What should I do? ~
Keep offering new foods without pressure, a tiny bit on his plate, and eat together as a family where you can.
He won't touch it. ~
It can take fifteen or twenty exposures. Don't bribe, don't argue, and don't make a separate meal every time.
I like dessert. ~
Dessert's fine, Ollie, as long as you try one bite of the green thing first. ~
One bite. Maybe. ~
Should he take vitamins? ~
A child multivitamin is reasonable, but not essential. I'd like to see him again in six weeks, to check his weight.
Six weeks. Thank you, doctor. ~

clinical_uncertainties.description: Child says the picky eating began two months ago; his mother says six months; summarised as two to six months, not confirmed.

clinical_actions.description: Keep offering new foods in tiny amounts without pressure and eat together
Do not bribe, argue or cook a separate meal each time

contradictions_detected: Duration of poor eating: patient two months vs family member six months (approximate range only).
